hybrid: filtered historical simulation: joint block resampling of volatility-standardized multi-asset residual vectors from regime-matched, split-disjoint development-lane block pools + Markov regime chain + GARCH-style volatility filter + bounded event overlays + jumps
notes: held-out variation: validation worlds use heavier event severity, noisier regime transitions and one extra event on average; sealed worlds use a wider severity range
drift_bias_correction_basis: re-estimated AFTER the variance moment-match: mean over 120 ENGINEERING worlds (ENG-DRIFTCAL2, indices 100-119 x 6 families) of [realized mean log return - drawn drift]
variance_scale_basis: all non-VNQ values inherited from the gen-v2 two-pass development-lane moment match; VNQ retuned from 0.7243 to 0.35 against the already-frozen 1256-session development-window target using only ENG-V5PROBE-GRID worlds

price_anchor.rationale: diversified ETFs hold baskets with earnings/valuation support; a pure random walk lets a single ETF lose 95% or gain 9x in 6 years, which the development lane never showed. The anchor is zero within a factor of ~2.5 of the world's starting level and pulls back beyond it.

repairs.V4-1: family anchor event inherited from gen-v3
repairs.V5-1: recession anchor minimum severity 0.9 prevents its normal headline event from being diluted below the unchanged family-exercise condition
repairs.V5-2: SPY direct event transmission 0.70 corrects excessive event-to-equity drawdown severity while leaving regime stress and the unchanged drawdown gates intact
repairs.V5-3: VNQ variance scale 0.35 and event transmission 0.75 correct excessive length-matched volatility
repairs.V5-4: GLD common-jump loading is asymmetric (0.80 down, 0.20 up) to reproduce the frozen negative-skew development target without altering admission tolerances
repairs.note: jump_neg_prob 0.55 inherited from gen-v2 (a post-hoc choice, disclosed)
